answer: Every identity carries a quartz clock: its receipt chains a delay keyed to each epoch beacon, so no head fast-forwards, and a compressed delay is rejected. Joining needs two identities whose horizon covers yours to countersign that delay; each may countersign once per epoch, so sponsors are scarce. A farm of n heads thus competes for n sponsor slots in one horizon; the clearing price rises per head, and each sponsor risks its bond if a protege fails. On an island made of fakes no valid countersignature exists, since no member's horizon predates its own cluster.
